questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. They wouldn't have hired you if you hadn't had some experience abroad.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

They wouldn't have hired you if you hadn't had some experience abroad.
questions.solution:
The given sentence is a conditional sentence. The basic structure of this type of sentence is

If + Past Participle, Past Participle.

The comma is removed when the sentence starts with the main clause like in the given sentence. The main clause follows the given structure. So, the conditional clause will be in past participle form. The underlined part is in past participle form and it is grammatically correct. So, no improvement is required in the given sentence. Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

Note:

Conditional Clause: A conditional clause is the one that usually starts with if or unless and describes something that is possible or probable. Example: If you're going to college, I could give you a lift. Here, "If you are going to the college" is the conditional clause and "I could give you a lift" is the main clause.

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. Since Monday, I am trying to reach him but he is neither responding to my calls nor replying to my messages.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

Since Monday, I am trying to reach him but he is neither responding to my calls nor replying to my messages.
questions.solution:
The error lies in option (b).

'Since' is a time expression that denotes a point of time.

The rule is: Present Indefinite + Time expression= Present Perfect.

For example: Monika has known me since 1995.

Similarly, in this question, 'Since' is a time expression. So, 'am trying' must be replaced by 'have been trying' (present perfect tense) in the sentence.

Thus, the error is in option (b) am trying.

Therefore, the corrected form of the sentence is: Since Monday, I have been trying to reach him but he is neither responding to my calls nor replying to my messages.

Additional Information:

Another important Time expression is 'For'.

'Since' denotes a period of time.

For example: Monika has known me for five months. ("five months" is a period of time)

questions.question: In the sentence, identify the segment that contains the grammatical error. By the time I reached at the event, the show started.
questions.questionHtml:
In the sentence, identify the segment that contains the grammatical error.

By the time I reached at the event, the show started.
questions.solution:
If two actions take places in the past, one after the other, 1st action will be in past perfect tense and the 2nd action will be in simple past tense. So 'the show had started' is the correct phrase.

Hence, option (d) is the correct choice.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Supposing that he had grasped the concept, he could do wonders in the new project.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Supposing that he had grasped the concept, he could do wonders in the new project.
questions.solution:
The tense in the 'Supposing that' clause should be in the Simple Past Tense (grasped) when the modal verb 'could' is in the main clause.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (a) he grasped.

The corrected form of the sentence is: Supposing that he grasped the concept, he could do wonders in the new project.

Additional Information:

'Supposing that' is a conditional sentence. The three types of conditional sentences (with examples) are given in the table.
ISupposing that I study (V1)I can pass the exam
IISupposing that I studied (V2)I could pass the exam
IIISupposing that I had studied (had + V3)I could have passed the exam

Hence, A is the right answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. It builds on previous work by advocacy groups and news organizations that _______ revealed the hidden ties between the industry and climate change sceptics.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

It builds on previous work by advocacy groups and news organizations that _______ revealed the hidden ties between the industry and climate change sceptics.
questions.solution:
The sentence is in present tense (evident by the use of 'builds' - present tense form of 'build') and hence, the use of 'was' and 'were' (past tense forms of 'be') will result in tense inconsistency. Options (b) and (d) can be negated based on this information. It is clear that we need a helping verb in place of the blank so as to make the present perfect tense construct (has/have + past participle of verb) indicating an already completed action that has present consequence/s. Also, the subject of this sentence is 'the previous work' - a singular noun - and hence, accordingly, we need to use a singular verb 'has' to fill in the blank.

The answer is option (c).

questions.question: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.
questions.questionHtml: Select the option with the correct use of future tense.

options.text: In two years, he will have work for this company for a decade.
options.html: In two years, he will have work for this company for a decade.

options.text: In two years, he will have worked for this company for a decade.
options.html: In two years, he will have worked for this company for a decade.

options.text: In two years, he will works for this company for a decade.
options.html: In two years, he will works for this company for a decade.

options.text: In two years, he will working for this company for a decade.
options.html: In two years, he will working for this company for a decade.

questions.solution:
The sentence uses the future perfect tense ("will have worked"), which is the correct form to indicate an action that will be completed by a certain point in the future. In this case, it means that in two years, the action of working for the company will be completed for a duration of ten years.

Option (a) is incorrect because "will have work" does not properly use the future perfect tense. The correct form is "will have worked."

Option (c) is incorrect because "will works" is grammatically incorrect. After "will," the base form of the verb ("work") should be used, not the third-person singular form ("works").

Option (d) is incorrect because "will working" is not a valid verb form in English. The correct form would be "will have worked" for the future perfect tense.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. After hearing their explanation,/ we understood that/ they had knew the/ consequences of their actions.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

After hearing their explanation,/ we understood that/ they had knew the/ consequences of their actions.
questions.solution:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is "they had knew the".

The error is related to the past tense verb "knew." The correct form should be "known," which is the past participle form of "know" (knew is the past tense form).

In the past perfect tense, the helping verb "had" is followed by the past participle form of the main verb (not by the past tense form).

Therefore, the correct phrase should be "they had known," not "they had knew." Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: After hearing their explanation, we understood that they had known the consequences of their actions.

Note:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the women fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. She promised that/ she would done/ everything possible to/ support the team.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

She promised that/ she would done/ everything possible to/ support the team.
questions.solution:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'she would done'.

The error is related to the verb "done."

When we form future conditional tense sentences with "would," we use the base form of the verb that follows "would."

The correct form in this case should be "do", not "done" [the past tense verb]. "Do" is the base form of the verb that should follow "would" to indicate the future action.

Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: She promised that she would do everything possible to support the team.

Option (a) is in the simple future tense ("will" + base form of the verb). Option (b) is in the present continuous tense ("is" + present participle). questions.question: Select the option that will improve the bracketed part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. Had she completed her homework, she (would have go) to the movies.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the bracketed part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Had she completed her homework, she (would have go) to the movies.
questions.solution:
Past conditional sentences, also known as the past unreal conditional or the third conditional, are used to talk about imaginary or hypothetical situations in the past and their possible outcomes.

'Had she completed her homework' is the past perfect clause, indicating an action (completing homework) that was supposed to be done before another past event.

Syntax: Had + subject + third form verb + object, subject + would have + third form verb.

Only option b) has the third form verb 'gone'. The given phrase and option a) have the base verb 'go', and option c) has 'been' which is not required.

The correct sentence is: Had she completed her homework, she would have gone to the movies.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the bracketed part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. By the time the guests (have arrived), we will have decorated the entire house for the party.
questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
When we use 'by the time' with the future perfect tense, we are expressing that an action will be completed, or a situation will have occurred before a specified future event.

Syntax: By the time, Simple Present tense, Future Perfect tense.

Only option d) is in the present tense. The given phrase is in present perfect tense, option a) is in present perfect continuous tense, and option b) is in simple future tense.

The correct sentence is: By the time the guests arrive, we will have decorated the entire house for the party.

Hence, option (d) is correct.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Generally, the pleasure / we took from / professional development / is often short-lived.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Generally, the pleasure / we took from / professional development / is often short-lived.
questions.solution:
Option (b) has an error. In part mentioned in option (b), the verb 'took' is in past tense form (V2) but the sentence is in Present tense [evident from 'generally' which implies the usual trend]. The verb mismatches with the tense of the sentence and it [took] must be replaced by the verb in Present tense form [take].

The correct sentence is: Generally, the pleasure we take from professional development is often short-lived.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

Note:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Tense: Grammatical tense tells us or expresses the time period that the action happens in. It can be happening now (present) or has happened already (past) or will happen later (future). Tenses help us understand how to use verbs correctly to indicate when the action took place.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Preeta wished she had not went to that party; it turned out to be quite boring.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Preeta wished she had not went to that party; it turned out to be quite boring.
questions.solution:
The segment that contains a grammatical error is 'had not went'. The error is related to the verb "went." The use of the helping verb "had" in the sentence indicates the past perfect tense. When constructing a sentence with the past perfect tense, the main verb is typically in the past participle form, not the simple past form. However, the verb "went" is in the simple past form, not the past participle form. Therefore, "went" should be replaced with its past participle form "gone" to maintain grammatical correctness in the past perfect tense construction. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Preeta wished she had not gone to that party; it turned out to be quite boring.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Walter White ventured into an illegal drug business with Jesse Pinkman after he ________ diagnosed with cancer so that he can leave behind a large fortune that can support his family in his absence.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Walter White ventured into an illegal drug business with Jesse Pinkman after he ________ diagnosed with cancer so that he can leave behind a large fortune that can support his family in his absence.
questions.solution:
- The correct option is (b) had been.

- The Past Perfect tense will be appropriate here.

- This tense is used when out of two actions it is necessary to emphasise that the preceding action was finished before the succeeding action started.

- Preceding actions are generally implied by the following as given below:

->After

->Recently

->Yet

- For example:

->I went to Mumbai after my father had returned home.

In the question, the first action was that Walter was diagnosed with cancer. The second action was that he ventured into an illegal business. The use of 'after' throws light on the fact that the preceding action was completely finished before the succeeding action started. Thus, the use of 'had been' is correct.

- The other options are grammatically incorrect.

- Therefore, the correct answer is: Walter White ventured into an illegal drug business with Jesse Pinkman after he had been diagnosed with cancer so that he can leave behind a large fortune that can support his family in his absence.

Additional Information:

- Past Perfect Tense used with certain verbs indicates that the action mentioned didn't take place. Some of the verbs are given below in the table:

->Want

->Hope

->Expect

->Think

- For example:

->I had wanted to go to Goa. (but couldn't go)
